statement: The first line holds n; the second holds n positive integers in a row. Pick any subset with no two picks adjacent and print the maximum possible sum. Carry two rolling values along the row: take, the best sum if the current element is picked (previous skipped), and skip, the best if it is passed. Update: new take is old skip plus the element; new skip is the better of the old pair. The answer is the better of the final pair.

example.why: 2 and 9 sit apart and sum to 11; taking the 4 blocks the 9 on one side.

hint: Two names, two lines of update - resist the urge for a whole array.
mistake: Picking alternate positions mechanically; value-aware skipping beats every fixed pattern.
